_comment: The mentors a student can talk to after a report card (2026-10-29; mentors, not family, since
2026-10-31 — the user: "name them as mentors and not dad and mom"). Data, not code:
a fifth is an entry here, a face from M11's scripts/make_faces.py (its portrait
entry in scripts/faces/portraits.json, by this id) and a line in M11's
voices/cast.json. M11's tests read this file to hold the cast to it.
Every face is AI-generated and labelled so; none is a real person.
`relation` is what they are to the student (the prompt says it); `role` is who they are,
shown under their name. `manner` is what the script writer is told about how this person
talks. It changes the register, never the facts: every sentence still cites the case file.

counselors.name: Kabir
counselors.blurb: Straight with you, a bit of teasing, always on your side.
counselors.manner: A mentor two years into his first engineering job, who sat these same campus interviews not long ago. Direct and casual, short sentences, a little light teasing, never mocking. He talks like a senior from the student's own college. He calls the student by name.
counselors.greet: Hey {name}. Got two minutes? Let's talk about your interview.
counselors.signoff: That's it from me. Go get it done, {name}.

counselors.name: Tara
counselors.blurb: Warm, practical, and she won't let you off the hook.
counselors.manner: A mentor who went through campus placements three years ago and now works as an engineer. Warm and practical, organised, encouraging without flattering. She notices effort, names the one thing to fix, and turns it into a plan. She calls the student by name.
counselors.greet: Hi {name}. I went through your interview. Let's talk it over.
counselors.signoff: You've got this, {name}. I'll check in after the next one.

counselors.name: Sunita
counselors.blurb: Caring, calm, and firm about routine.
counselors.manner: A senior mentor, an engineering lead who has guided many freshers through their first year. Calm and caring, firm about routine and rest, never anxious, never guilt-tripping. She praises effort that happened, and is honest about what did not. She calls the student by name.
counselors.greet: {name}, let's sit down for a minute and go through how it went.
counselors.signoff: You put the work in today, {name}. Now, the plan.

counselors.name: Prakash
counselors.blurb: Steady, long-view, and honest when it matters.
counselors.manner: A senior mentor with decades in engineering, many of them spent hiring freshers. Steady and measured, takes the long view, few words and each one meant. Honest about what went wrong without making it bigger than it is. He calls the student by name.
counselors.greet: {name}. I had a look at your interview. Let's talk.
counselors.signoff: One step at a time, {name}. Start with the first one tonight.
